A.explanation: This uses 42% as the submerged fraction. The submerged fraction is $100\% - 42\% = 58\%$, so this value is too small.

B.explanation: This is close to $7900 \times 0.58$. The mercury density must be larger than iron density because most of the iron is supported while submerged, so multiply by $1/0.58$ not $0.58$.

C.explanation: Weight equals upthrust, so $\rho_{iron}V = \rho_{mercury} \times 0.58V$, giving $\rho_{mercury} \approx 13600 \text{ kg m}^{-3}$, closest to $14000 \text{ kg m}^{-3}$.

D.explanation: This is larger than the correct ratio suggests. It does not follow from dividing $7900 \text{ kg m}^{-3}$ by the $0.58$ submerged fraction.

hints: Notice that 42% of the iron cube volume is above mercury, so calculate the fraction actually submerged and displacing mercury.
Connect floating in equilibrium to weight of the whole cube balancing the upthrust from the displaced mercury.
Rearrange $\rho_{iron}Vg = \rho_{mercury}V_{sub}g$ to find mercury density from $7900 \text{ kg m}^{-3}$ divided by the submerged fraction.
walkthrough: Find the submerged volume fraction. With 42% above the surface, the fraction below is $1 - 0.42 = 0.58$, so $V_{sub} = 0.58V$ where $V$ is the cube volume.
State the floating condition. In equilibrium the weight down equals the Archimedes upthrust up: $\rho_{iron}Vg = \rho_{mercury}V_{sub}g$.
Cancel $V$ and $g$ to get the density relation: $\rho_{mercury} = \rho_{iron} \times V/V_{sub} = \rho_{iron}/0.58$.
Substitute $\rho_{iron} = 7900 \text{ kg m}^{-3}$: $\rho_{mercury} = 7900/0.58 \approx 13620 \text{ kg m}^{-3}$ with unit $\text{kg m}^{-3}$.
Round sensibly for multiple choice. $13620 \text{ kg m}^{-3}$ is closest to $14000 \text{ kg m}^{-3}$. This is option C.
